reasoning_trace: Listed pr/head/evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/: MANIFEST.json, prs/, regen.sh, suite.yaml, tasks/ — no runs/. Ran the first test of each suite in a scratch copy: both fail in setup() with cp: cannot stat .../ablation-runs/runs. bats-tests.yml:213-222 runs bats evals/tests/ and exits 1 on failure.
finding: The two new eval suites (18 + 21 tests) consume a fixture directory the PR does not ship, so every test fails in setup and the PR's own CI step goes red.
critique: regen.sh:52-56 writes runs/ and :86-89 prunes gitignored files; the directories were never committed.
remediation: Run evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/regen.sh after the jq fix and commit evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/, or regenerate in setup() when absent.

reasoning_trace: jq 1.6 on this host: `jq -n --arg label x '$label'` -> syntax error, unexpected label; `{label: 1} | {label}` -> syntax error; printf a b c NUL-joined | jq -Rs 'split("\u0000") | .[:-1]' -> ["a","b"]. Ran pipeline-run.bats A4 case with output surfaced: rc=2, jq compile error at the argv capture, pipeline.json status infrastructure_error, phases 0. ablation-row.sh:285 uses the {name, label, ...} shorthand.
finding: The executor and the row builder require jq >= 1.7: on jq 1.6 (the repository's stated floor, .claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:208; Debian 12) every phase aborts before it starts and no row can be built; after a variable rename the NUL split still drops the last argv/env element, so took-effect rules A4/A6/A7 read false evidence.
critique: Four jq programs depend on 1.7-only syntax or semantics; the CI runner (ubuntu-latest, jq 1.7.1) hides it.
remediation: Rename the jq variable (--arg lbl), spell `label: .label`, and build arrays with `jq -n --args '$ARGS.positional' "${cargv[@]}"`; add a bats case pinning `argv | length == ${#cargv[@]}` or a jq version guard.

reasoning_trace: The PR changes 17 tracked .claude/ files (model-config.yaml, check-loa.sh, preflight.sh, generated-model-maps.sh, CLAUDE.loa.md, bridgebuilder dist, test_pricing_resolution_ladder.py) and adds a CI step that regenerates the manifest from the tracked tree and exits 1 on any differing path (gen-checksums.sh:152-168). head.diff carries no .claude/checksums.json; only model-config.yaml.checksum was refreshed. tests/unit/check-manifest-paths.bats:88-92 (MP-6) asserts the manifest is committed. The upstream tree is outside the snapshot, hence medium confidence.
finding: The new integrity gate fails on this PR's own tree, and every fresh downstream mount of the merged commit reports Tampered for each changed .claude/ path — the #1267 symptom class the PR exists to end.
critique: The gate and the manifest must land in the same commit; tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh --worktree would have shown it.
remediation: Run bash tools/gen-checksums.sh on the final tree and commit .claude/checksums.json; run tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh --worktree and record the summary line in the report.

reasoning_trace: The manifest is generated from git ls-files (gen-checksums.sh:102) and the count is now taken from git ls-files too, so both sides are index entries: a tracked file deleted from disk and an untracked file planted under .claude/hooks/ or .claude/scripts/ both leave ACTUAL_COUNT unchanged. The replaced find count (:196, now only when the tracked count is 0) saw both. Confirmed by cross-model review (DISS-C-001) and the review's DISS-001.
finding: The preflight System Zone count check no longer inspects the filesystem: it only detects a stale manifest, never on-disk drift in either direction.
critique: check-loa.sh still fails a deleted manifest path as Missing, but nothing flags a planted untracked executable at preflight.
remediation: Count tracked paths that exist (`git ls-files -- .claude | while read f; do [[ -e $f ]] && ...`) and compare the on-disk find count against the tracked count as a second signal, or call check_integrity outright.

reasoning_trace: submodule_mount is the heuristic [[ -d .loa/.claude ]] (:64). Upstream holds every manifest path, so in a submodule mount an absent path is always informational not-mounted and Missing can never fire; a removed link to a hook or gate script is indistinguishable from a by-design unlinked path. The heuristic is also satisfiable in a non-submodule mount by creating .loa/.claude/ plus a shadow copy. DISS-C-002 part 2 (`return 0` hides drift) is not a defect: fail() increments FAILURES (:36) and main exits 1 when FAILURES > 0 (:603-605); the base's trailing `[[ ]] && log` returned 1 and aborted the script under set -e.
finding: In submodule mode the integrity check degrades to a Tampered-only check; deletion of a linked System Zone file is never reported as Missing.
critique: The outcome is the #1267 design decision, but it should be compared against the mount's own link list rather than against existence upstream.
remediation: Record the set of linked paths at mount time (mount-submodule.sh) and treat an absent path that is in that set as Missing; keep not-mounted for paths outside it.

reasoning_trace: rule_integrity_clean verifies every manifest entry against the sandbox's current checksums.json but only annotates when that file's digest equals arm_evidence.manifest_sha256 recorded at materialisation (pipeline-run.sh:492-493). A phase that edits .claude/ and regenerates the manifest (hooks, update.sh, tools/gen-checksums.sh can) verifies clean against its own manifest.
finding: The recorded manifest digest is captured as a pin but never enforced, so a sandbox whose .claude/ was rewritten and re-manifested passes integrity_clean.
critique: The evidence line names the pin; the rule should fail on it.
remediation: [[ "$filesha" == "$msha" ]] || { EVID="manifest replaced since materialisation ($filesha vs $msha)"; return 1; }

code_snippet:
for f in auth.json config.toml; do
  if [[ -f "$CREDS_HOME/.codex/$f" ]]; then cp "$CREDS_HOME/.codex/$f" "$HOME_DIR/.codex/$f"; fi
done
reasoning_trace: HOME_DIR=$META/home (:301) sits inside the run directory under evals/results/. finish() (:348) and on_exit() (:356) remove it, but a SIGKILL or OOM kill of the driver runs no trap (the header :104-106 anticipates a SIGKILLed driver). The codex OAuth credential then stays in the results tree that batches archive.
finding: An operator credential (~/.codex/auth.json) is copied into the results tree and can persist after an abnormal driver exit.
critique: Only the regular exit paths clean up; nothing sweeps stale meta/home/ on the next start.
remediation: Stage the codex files in a mktemp -d outside the run directory (bind-mount that), or chmod 0600 and sweep */meta/home/ at driver start; never store credentials under the archived results tree.

reasoning_trace: regen_sandbox_manifest executes tools/gen-checksums.sh from the prompt tree when it is executable and the sandbox is a git work tree tracking .claude files (:384-386). gen-checksums.sh sources its own tree's .claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh (:51). In execute-agent.sh EVAL_PROMPT_TREE is the tree under evaluation (:146), i.e. the PR in the eval.yml model that the header (:96-100) says must never run in the harness. The bats trust-boundary scan (pipeline-run.bats:248-260) checks four files and `source` lines only, so neither this exec nor init_sandbox_beads' bash of the sandbox's update-beads-state.sh (:513) is covered. Current callers rarely satisfy the git condition, hence medium confidence.
finding: The trusted harness can execute code from the tree under evaluation (and the script it sources) when the sandbox tracks .claude files, contradicting the harness's own trust-boundary rule.
critique: The inline hashlib path already produces an equivalent manifest; the external tool adds a boundary crossing for no gain.
remediation: Always use the inline hashlib generator (drop the `$tool` branch), or copy gen-checksums.sh from the harness repo only (never $EVAL_PROMPT_TREE); extend the trust-boundary bats scan to lib/sandbox-mount.sh and to direct executions of prompt-tree paths.

reasoning_trace: init_sandbox_beads probes br on the driver host; Dockerfile.ablation:82-84 says the image has no br and expects the opt-out marker; pipeline-run.sh never sets LOA_EVAL_BR_BIN. An operator with br on PATH gives every containerised arm a .beads/ database the in-container CLI cannot drive; one without gives the opt-out marker.
finding: Sandbox beads state depends on the driver host's PATH, not on the arm, so arm parity varies by operator machine.
critique: The evidence line records br|opt-out|none, but nothing pins it per executor mode.
remediation: In container mode pass LOA_EVAL_BR_BIN=/nonexistent (or probe the image) so every arm gets the same beads state; assert the value in took-effect or the row.

reasoning_trace: Neither paths list (:23-46 push, :49-72 pull_request) names evals/**, tools/gen-checksums.sh, tools/check-manifest-paths.sh or tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh, yet the workflow now runs the eval harness suites (:213-225) and the manifest gate (:176-179).
finding: A change limited to the harness, its tests or the manifest tools never triggers the steps that gate them.
critique: The gates exist but are not reachable from the code they protect.
remediation: Add evals/**, tools/gen-checksums.sh, tools/check-manifest-paths.sh and tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh to both paths lists.

reasoning_trace: bats-tests.yml:11-16 states the repository's pinning policy (exact versions + integrity verification; the workflow verifies the bats-core commit SHA at :147-152 and the yq sha256). The image installs four Python packages by lower-bound range (:69), clones bats-core by mutable tag without the SHA check (:72-74) and installs the two CLIs by version without integrity (:60-63). The image is the batch's fixed identity (drift_guard, ablation-2.0.yaml:86), so two builds can differ.
finding: The ablation image departs from the repository's pinning policy for its Python deps and bats-core, so rebuilds are not reproducible and a tag move or a new dependency release changes the batch toolchain silently.
critique: The yq install in the same file shows the intended pattern.
remediation: Pin exact versions (and hashes via a requirements file with --require-hashes), verify the bats-core commit SHA as the workflow does, and record `pip freeze` in the image health check.

reasoning_trace: Operator-specific fallback path under $HOME in shared code; $HOME under set -u; tool_version executes it when present (:60-62). pipeline-run.sh:428 swallows a failure (|| echo "") and records fingerprint null. Confirmed by cross-model review DISS-C-005.
finding: The fingerprint executes a binary from a user-writable, operator-specific path and silently records null when the script fails.
critique: A missing bats should read bats=absent, as the header promises for other tools.
remediation: Drop the dotfiles fallback (bats=absent when not on PATH) and make pipeline-run.sh fail or warn when fingerprint.sh exits non-zero.

reasoning_trace: Header :125-126 states no .claude/ code is run by the harness; price_for executes pricing.py from the harness repo's .claude/adapters. REPO_ROOT is the harness's own tree (trusted copy), so this is a documentation/invariant mismatch rather than a boundary crossing; the bats scan (pipeline-run.bats:248-260) only inspects source lines and would not catch an exec.
finding: The harness executes .claude/ code despite its stated invariant, and the invariant's test cannot see executions.
critique: Either the invariant or the code should change; the test should cover both.
remediation: Document the exception (trusted-copy pricing) or read prices from a harness-owned table; extend the trust-boundary scan to python3/bash invocations of .claude/ paths.

code_snippet: # PLACEHOLDER: gpt-5.5 list prices copied 2026-10-15 until the gpt-6.1 rate card is confirmed
reasoning_trace: gpt-6.1-sol pricing (:144-149) is an acknowledged placeholder; codex-headless cli_model now points at it (:240) so every codex estimate and MODELINV row prices through it with no provisional marker on the rows. The entry's fallback_chain is openai:codex-headless (:135), whose cli_model is gpt-6.1-sol, so an API-key failure silently re-runs the request through the operator's ChatGPT subscription (cross-model DISS-C-006; review DISS-C-003).
finding: Placeholder pricing flows into cost rows unmarked, and the HTTP entry's fallback crosses into the subscription credential path on API errors.
critique: The within-company chain is the repository convention, but the placeholder should be visible where it is consumed.
remediation: Add a pricing_note/provisional flag that pricing.py surfaces on rows, or price the hop as unknown until the rate card lands; track the bead named in the comment.

reasoning_trace: ablation-row.sh:276 falls back to $m.source_commit; the row would carry the literal placeholder when pipeline.json lacks the field.
finding: Placeholder commit id in the suite file can reach runs.jsonl.
critique: A validator rule for a 7-40 hex commit id would catch it.
remediation: Set the commit before the freeze and have validate-suite.sh reject a non-hex source_commit.

reasoning_trace: -type f skips symlinks and empty directories, so a symlinked fixture file is outside the frozen identity and can change without drift.
finding: The suite freeze does not cover symlinks.
critique: Refuse symlinks under tasks/ or hash their targets.
remediation: Add `-o -type l` with a refusal, or `find -L`.

reasoning_trace: docker run --memory 4g (:688) OOM-kills the CLI with exit 137 before the timeout; the driver classes it interrupted (exit 4) rather than agent_error.
finding: A model that blows the memory cap reads as an operator interrupt and is excluded from the analysis as interrupted.
critique: Distinguish the container's OOMKilled flag from a signal.
remediation: Inspect `docker inspect --format '{{.State.OOMKilled}}'` before --rm removes the container (drop --rm and remove manually), or treat 137 without a driver signal as agent_error.

reasoning_trace: degraded, degraded_reason and voices_run derive from envelopes read first from the agent-writable sandbox; effort_effective and voice_cost_usd derive from eval/model-invoke.jsonl, which pipeline-run.sh copies out of the agent-writable sandbox/.eval (:773). The header's never-from-sandbox rule (DEC-0413) is applied to the arm only. Cross-model DISS-C-003 rated this MEDIUM; kept LOW because the forging party is the Loa agent under test, not an adversary, and took-effect rules bound the effect.
finding: Row quality fields are derived from artefacts the system under measurement can write.
critique: Prefer the eval/ copies and record their provenance.
remediation: Read envelopes from eval/ only (the copy taken right after each gate phase) and mark rows whose sandbox and eval copies differ.

code_snippet: select(type == "object" and .type == "tool_use" and (.name == "Write" or .name == "Edit" or .name == "MultiEdit" or .name == "NotebookEdit"))
reasoning_trace: zone_violations.dot_claude_writes counts only four tool names; Bash-tool writes (echo >, sed -i, cp), symlinks into .claude/ and nested foo/.claude/ paths are not recorded (cross-model DISS-C-004). integrity_clean catches content changes to manifest-listed files, so the gap is in attribution, not detection.
finding: System Zone writes made through the Bash tool are absent from zone_violations.
critique: Known Loa fence gap (CLAUDE.loa.md: Bash-path App-Zone writes are review-territory); the metric should say so.
remediation: Also scan Bash tool_use commands for .claude/ redirections and in-place edits, or derive the metric from a snapshot diff of .claude/ per phase.

code_snippet: ledger_micro="$(printf '%s\n' "$ledger_rows" | jq -R -n '[inputs | fromjson? | select(type == "object") | (.cost_micro_usd // ((.cost_usd // 0) * 1000000))] | add // 0 | round' ...
reasoning_trace: sandbox/.eval/cost-ledger.jsonl is writable by the agent under test; rows are summed into SPENT_MICRO (:854) with no non-negative or numeric clamp. A negative or non-numeric cost_micro_usd row lowers the recorded spend and defers cap_failure (:864); a huge one triggers it.
finding: The per-run spend cap trusts ledger rows the sandbox agent can write.
critique: The CLI's result.total_cost_usd is authoritative; the ledger should only add.
remediation: Clamp each row to a non-negative number (`select(type == "number" and . >= 0)`) and count rows by cheval's primitive_id shape only.
